notes: §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR5 (ALL FORMATS, as Amendment 1 words it): 'If any identifier is subscripted or is a function-identifier, the subscript or function-identifier is evaluated only once as the first operation in the execution of the INSPECT statement.' No edition arm: every edition runs InspectEmitter.Emit, whose first act is IdentifyOperands, which freezes the subscripts (and reference modifiers) of identifier-1, each TALLYING counter, pattern and BEFORE/AFTER delimiter, each REPLACING pattern, replacement and delimiter and the CONVERTING operands into locals, in source order, through PlaceIdentification.Freeze; TallyOperandTexts evaluates each TALLYING function-identifier once into a local before any counter is stored. Conforms for: a subscript on every data-item operand class in formats 1 to 4 (probes: counter as subscript of identifier-1, of a pattern, of a delimiter, of a format 3 REPLACING operand, relative subscript), and a function-identifier in TALLYING or as identifier-1 (the witness: COUNTER, SUBJECT, OPERAND, FUNCTION lines). Does NOT conform for a function-identifier in the REPLACING half of a format 3 statement: PlaceIdentification.Freeze returns a non-field operand unchanged, and EmitBody renders it (OperandTextOf) inline in the InspectReplace call, after the TALLYING counters are stored, so the function and the subscripts of its arguments are evaluated after the format 1 half ran. Freeze's comment that a function's argument subscripts 'were hoisted at bind time' holds only for a function-bearing subscript (StatementBinder.SubscriptSegments), not for a plain subscript on an argument. The result is wrong on either reading of format 3: GR5 puts the function first in 'the INSPECT statement', and §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR17 ('as though two successive INSPECT statements') still requires 'Subscripting associated with any identifier in the format 2 statement is evaluated only once before executing the format 1 statement'. A function whose unsubscripted argument the counter changes (C1 REDEFINES X1; TALLYING C1 ... REPLACING ALL FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (X1)) is read after the tally too: right on the two-statement reading of GR17, wrong on GR5's own wording; the repro avoids that doubt. --std 2023 prints the same, where §2023:14.9.22.4 GR19 ('Item identification of any identifier in the format 2 statement is done only once before executing the format 1 statement') leaves no doubt: a lead against the 2023 rows GR-14.9.22.4-6 and GR-14.9.22.4-19. The occurs-depending length of a format 3 identifier-1 is not this rule (GR5 names subscripts and function-identifiers only); it is GR17's and is kb/Work PB5119.

next.reason: Amendment 1 (X3.23a-1989) added function-identifiers to 'Subscripting associated with any identifier is evaluated only once'; Amendment 2 renumbered the rule (old GR4). §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR5: 'the subscript or function-identifier is evaluated only once as the first operation'. §2023:14.9.22.4 GR6: 'Item identification for any identifier is done only once as the first operation', and §2023:14.6.4 lists its steps: 'function evaluation' and 'subscript evaluation' (kept), 'reference modification' (no change: §1985:IV.4.3.8 already has 'any subscripting and reference modification are evaluated only once as the first operation of the execution of that statement') and 'length evaluation for an occurs-depending group item', the case added. 1985 takes that length 'at the start of the operation' (§1985:VI.5.8.4 GR3) and runs format 3 'as though two successive INSPECT statements', fixing before the first only 'Subscripting associated with any identifier in the format 2 statement' (§1985:VI.6.18.4 GR17). So INSPECT G TALLYING N FOR ... REPLACING ..., N the DEPENDING ON item of G, replaces over G's new length in 1985 and over its first length in 2023 (§2023:14.9.22.4 GR19: 'Item identification of any identifier in the format 2 statement is done only once').
